title: AI Design Suite — per-project component maturity tags
description: Schema for a consuming project's own component-maturity file (conventionally .design-suite/component-maturity.json, pointed to by profile.json's componentMaturity.file). This is deliberately NOT the same vocabulary as this suite's own proven/unverified/experimental/pointer tier in CLAUDE.md and catalog.py: that one is gated on an evidence file naming what ran, when, and against which project (docs/ROADMAP.md Workstream A2) because it grades THIS SUITE'S OWN audits and skills against a mechanised check. A consuming project's UI components (a Flutter DsButton, a React Table) have no such check to gate against, and forcing the same evidence requirement onto them would just move the 'proven is a word someone typed' problem down one level. This schema instead uses a stability vocabulary a design system already reasons in day to day, and leaves evidence optional and free-text rather than gated. `status` is required precisely so a project cannot half-populate this file: an entry that exists but forgot to say how mature it is is exactly the ambiguity this schema exists to remove.

status.description: Stability of a component's public API, from the consuming project's own judgement. Not the suite's proven/unverified/experimental/pointer tier — see the file-level description. `stable`: safe to build on, breaking changes are deliberate and communicated. `experimental`: API may change without notice; callers should expect churn. `deprecated`: still present but scheduled for removal — `supersededBy` should usually be set. `unverified`: exists and is used, but nobody has reviewed its API surface. Treat an UNTAGGED component (absent from this file entirely) as unverified too, never as stable by default — an audit that cannot find an entry must say so, not assume the best case.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the component's source file, for tooling that wants to resolve the tag to a file without re-deriving it from the key.

since.description: Free text: a version, a date, or a release name — whatever the project already uses to mark 'introduced in'.

owner.description: Team or individual who can answer questions about this component. Free text, not an email address — keep real identities out of a file that gets committed and read by tooling.

supersededBy.description: The component key that replaces this one. Meaningful mainly on a `deprecated` entry.

notes.description: Why this status, in one sentence. Optional, but a status with no reasoning is exactly the assertion-not-evidence problem this file exists to avoid repeating.

evidence.description: Optional pointers to what backs this status — a test file, a design review doc, a usage audit output. Free-text paths or URLs, deliberately not gated the way the suite's own `proven` tier is: see the file-level description for why.

components.description: Keyed by however the project names its own components — a Flutter class name (`DsButton`), a React export (`Table`), a path-qualified name if the project has collisions (`forms/Button`). The key is opaque to this schema; whatever a project's tooling already uses to identify a component is fine as long as it is used consistently, because that key is what other tooling (an audit annotating promotion candidates, a doc generator) will look up.
